summary: ```markdown # CLO Technique Teaching Workshop: How to Showcase Strap Wear ## Introduction In this workshop, we will explore the process of showcasing strap wear using various modeling techniques. The aim is to create realistic strap effects on a model, demonstrating different methods of sewing and positioning straps. ## Preparing the Strap First of all, this strap is already worn on the model, but it has a slightly stretched shape when worn. So, we will select the strap version, open it, and switch the strap type to a harder type before simulating it. ### Simulation of Strap After simulation, you can see that the strap is not deformed and is worn on the model. Now, we turn to the back of the model to create the ring of the strap. ## Creating the Ring Plate ### Step 1: Shape Tool First, we use the shape tool to create a ring plate and enter a suitable size. Then we sew the plate to the position of the back piece. ### Step 2: Positioning After sewing, we switch to the tool, add to the side at the 3D window, and quickly arrange the board in a position near the model. We can use the positioning ball to move the board. ### Step 3: Folding the Panel Next, we need to add an inner line in the middle of this panel to fold it. Before we fold it, we will harden this panel. After hardening, we can model it and level it. After leveling, use the folding arrangement tool to create a fold for it. Change the fold angle to 0, and then sew it. Remember to change the model type to TURN. ### Step 4: Adjusting the Panel After modeling, because this panel is very small, we will reduce its particle diameter, and the thickness of the gap will also be reduced. Remove its hardening. We want this panel to be a little bit rounder, so we change the inner line angle to 180 degrees. If you want it to be rounder, you can increase the folding strength to maintain the 180-degree angle. ## Sewing Fixation Now we need to make a sewing fixation on this part of the strap. First, remove the previous sewing line. After removing it, we place the other side of the panel on the opposite side, giving it a colon to indicate symmetrical panels. Then, freeze the back of our back. The strap panel can also be frozen. After modeling, we will activate the two straps. ## Sewing the Panels After activating, we need to sew it on the panel of the belt we made. If you can't find the right position while sewing, you can view it in 3D and slightly adjust its position. ### Adjusting the Panels The example of these two panels can also be reduced to three. Once sewn onto the board of our two belts, we will add a sticky layer in the middle. We still need a belt of a belt to come over, so we have to continue creating a new board. Then, we need to measure the length of this new board using our measuring tool. ### Step 5: Measuring the New Board One-click start and double-click end to measure the length of this section. You can see that this length is now more than 127. Then, we create a 130mm board. ### Step 6: Creating the New Board What about this height? Since there was no measurement just now, let's measure it again using our editing board tool. The width of our belt is 7.9, so we can create a new board with a height of 8. ## Finalizing the Board Position After the installation is done, we arrange this board quickly to the back of our model. You can see that there is an arrow tool on our positioning ball. After we click on this tool, the board will move with your mouse to your designated position. ### Adjusting the Position Then we use the positioning ball to adjust its position. We make an example modification to the building and add our tape, then sew it. When sewing, we can check the corresponding relationship between 3D and 2D to avoid sewing it incorrectly. ### Step 7: Correcting the Sewing Line If we sew it the other way around, we can switch the direction of the sewing line with the ice sewing line tool. After moving it to the middle, we make this board left and right symmetrical using the plus point division tool to add two straight points in the middle of our board. ## Completing the First Method After selecting this board, we right-click and set it to left and right symmetry. This way, the sewing line is automatically added. Click on the simulation, and our first method of wearing a ring is almost complete. This method is a more stable one; it's actually a fake wear, not a real wear, but sewn onto this board. ### Adjusting the Sewing Line Visibility To remove the effect of the sewing line, we can use the editor sewing line tool, select this set of sewing lines, and adjust the strength of the sewing line in the attribute editor to 0, making it invisible. We will adjust the sewing line to the middle position for a more realistic appearance as it is fixed from above. ## Second Method: Real Wear Now let's talk about the second way of making, which is our real wear. First, we delete the fixed sewing line and hide this board using Shift + Q. ### Step 8: Sewing the Boards Together After selecting that board, we can sew these two boards together in 3D. After sewing, we use Shift + W to show all our boards and adjust the position of our board to be in the middle of our ring for sewing. ### Adjusting and Finalizing the Real Wear If we simulate it directly, there may be some problems, so we can undo and adjust this position again. The middle of the board can be pulled closer. After shifting back, we can remove the big body freeze to observe the structure of the ring clearly. ### Step 9: Final Adjustments If we add to it and simulate, it will still go through. Therefore, we need to switch to different sticky types for better stability. Finally, we will optimize this area by using the edge sewing line tool to remove the hairline intensity. We will also add a butterfly knot at the end of this place. ## Conclusion In conclusion, we have successfully showcased strap wear through two different methods: fake wear and real wear. Each approach has its unique applications and can be optimized further for different design needs. You can simulate it after wearing it, and then bring it over in a simulated state. To fix its position, we can use our sewing needle tool to click on one of our butterfly-shaped panels and then click on the inner-layer panel to fix it. After adjustment, we simulate to achieve the butterfly knot effect, completing our workshop on showcasing strap wear. ```
